method: Three rounds of 5 random generated items per chapter (65 items each, 195 in all, across bank, practice forms and mocks) re-solved by hand: every numerical (ploidy, Mendelian and Hardy-Weinberg ratios, recombination, DNA length and H-bonds, PCR copies, restriction fragments, population change, exponential/logistic growth, NPP, 10% law, species-area Z) recomputed from the stem data, every fact/MCQ key checked against NCERT Biology XII
fixes: evolution: 'disruptive selection' was keyed as NOT a factor that disturbs Hardy-Weinberg equilibrium (it is a form of natural selection, which does); the overlapping 'type of natural selection' group was replaced by origin-of-life ideas
populations: 'Which is a factor that increases population density?' offered both natality and birth rate; group replaced by indirect census methods (pug marks, faecal pellets, fish per trap)
conservation: the hotspot 'Indo-Burma' appeared as a wrong option for in situ conservation (hotspot protection is in situ); group replaced by causes of biodiversity loss
linkage: recombination frequency 10/800 printed as 1.2% instead of 1.25%; now given to two decimals
apomixis: 'citrus (orange)' was a wrong option for a parthenocarpic fruit although seedless navel oranges are parthenocarpic; replaced by jamun (Syzygium) in the polyembryony group
keys: answers inserted mid-sentence were capitalised ('controls Corn borer', 'is a Oral contraceptive'); fact-table keys now keep case and avoid the bad article
wording: decomposition stem for humification, birth-rate stem tense, hominid label 'Ramapithecus (and Dryopithecus)', species-area Z item now uses whole-number species counts
note: Five keys were wrong or ambiguous (all fixed); no other wrong answers found. Bank regenerated and revalidated after the fixes.
